finding: T21's single read of 0x795fe3dd was NOT a first-bring-up/session artifact. It reproduces with zero variance across 6 independent reset-reconfigure-run cycles and 96 total AHB-bank observations (0 of 96 exceptions), with FCB_STAT 0x000f0002 confirmed every cycle (the fabric did configure each time) and a DEVICE_ID sanity read of 0x40200001 confirmed every cycle (the DAP/AHB read path itself is sane -- it returns a different, correct value at a different address, so it is not simply stuck or globally broken). Both config-time determinism (across the 6 reconfigures) and read-time determinism (12 back-to-back direct reads within one configuration, no intervening reset) are total. This closes the session-glitch hypothesis raised in T21/T22: the mismatch is real and stable on this physical L64 unit for this exact bitstream. It does NOT by itself resolve T22's open question of where the fault sits (a toolchain/bitgen-encoding bug that would also reproduce on L48, versus something L64-package- or silicon-specific) -- T22 already showed every desk-computable layer of this exact bitstream (cycle-sim, routed-JSON pip-tree reconstruction against mcu_hrdata_lanes.csv, bitgen's cross-net mux-ownership check) independently agrees the intended encoding is 0x4147414d, and nothing new was added at that layer this session. The decisive discriminator is still the L48 hardware re-read, which still could not be run: only the L64 unit is physically attached (reconfirmed fresh this session by 16KiB flash-prefix hash).

method: one continuous OpenOCD session (single process, no re-attach between cycles) running 6 full reset-bracketed cycles. Each cycle: reset halt, then load_image the fabric bin at 0x20002000, load_image the firmware bin at 0x20000000, set pc/sp, resume, sleep 500ms, halt, mdw the firmware's 8-word mailbox at 0x20001000 (FCB_STAT, BANK+0x0, BANK+0x4, BANK+0x40, post-write-readback of BANK+0x0, a stability flag versus the hardcoded 0x4147414d expectation, a completion sentinel, one unused word), mdw the known-good DEVICE_ID address 0x03000100 once as a read-path sanity check, then 12 further direct mdw reads of AHB 0x60000000 with no reconfigure in between (in-config read-time check). After all 6 cycles: a plain reset (flash-boot) plus shutdown. Zero flash writes at any point in this trial (including the board-identification dump above, which is read-only)
observed_reads_breakdown: per cycle: 4 mailbox-embedded BANK reads (BANK+0x0, BANK+0x4, BANK+0x40, post-write-readback of BANK+0x0) plus 12 direct in-config reads of BANK+0x0, totalling 16 per cycle times 6 cycles = 96 total observations of the AHB bank, all identical
scope: Establishes L64-side reproducibility beyond any reasonable doubt (deterministic, 0 of 96 exceptions, FCB and read-path sanity both confirmed): this was a real, stable silicon/toolchain result, not a bring-up glitch. Makes no claim about L48 and no claim about which layer (silicon conduction vs. toolchain bitgen encoding) is responsible; that attribution needs the L48 hardware rerun.
